A kennel is a shelter made specifically for a dog. Think of it as a dog's own personal house — a small, enclosed structure where a dog sleeps, rests, and stays safe from rain, cold, or harsh sun. It is almost always placed outdoors, in a yard or garden.

Picture a small wooden box with a slanted roof, an opening at the front for the dog to walk in and out, and just enough space for the dog to lie down comfortably. That is a kennel. The dog does not share it with humans — it belongs entirely to the dog.

1. A dog's individual shelter (the "dog house" sense)

This is the most basic meaning. A kennel here refers to a single, small structure — usually made of wood, plastic, or metal — where one dog lives or sleeps. It is what most people picture when they hear the word.

"He built a wooden kennel for his Labrador in the backyard."
"The dog ran straight into its kennel when it started raining."

The key idea: it is a private, dedicated space for one dog, usually outdoors.

2. A place or business that houses multiple dogs (the "facility" sense)

A kennel can also refer to an establishment — a place run by people — where several dogs are kept, looked after, bred, or trained professionally.

There are different types of such places:

  • Boarding kennels: When you go on a vacation and cannot take your dog along, you leave it at a boarding kennel. The staff there feed it, walk it, and take care of it until you return. Think of it as a hotel — but for dogs.

    "We dropped Biscuit off at the kennels before flying to Paris."

  • Breeding kennels: A place where dogs are bred (i.e., mated to produce puppies) and raised, usually with the goal of selling the puppies or maintaining a particular breed.

    "She bought her Border Collie from a reputable kennel in the countryside."

  • Training kennels: Some establishments focus on training dogs — teaching them commands, discipline, or skills (like police dogs or guide dogs). These are also called kennels.

In everyday speech, when people say "I'm putting my dog in kennels" or "the kennels", they almost always mean a boarding facility — a temporary home for their dog.
Singular vs. Plural — A Subtle but Important Point

• "A kennel" (singular) → usually means the individual dog shelter (the small hut in the yard).
  • "A kennel" (singular) → can also refer to a single business/facility, especially when named: "Golden Paws Kennel" or "she owns a kennel".
  • "Kennels" (plural) → almost always refers to the facility/establishment, especially in British English. "The kennels" = the boarding or breeding place.

"The kennel in the garden needs repainting." — the dog's little house.
"The dog is at the kennels this week." — the boarding facility.

• Kennel club: An official organization that registers dog breeds, sets breed standards, and organizes dog shows. The most famous ones are the American Kennel Club (AKC) and the Kennel Club in the UK.
  • Kennel cough: A highly contagious respiratory infection in dogs — named so because it spreads easily in kennels where many dogs live close together.
  • Kennel run: An enclosed outdoor area, usually fenced with wire, attached to a kennel or boarding facility, where dogs can move around, exercise, and relieve themselves safely without escaping.

• It is not a cage (a cage is a wire or metal enclosure, usually used temporarily — at the vet, during travel, or for brief confinement). A kennel is more like a permanent or semi-permanent shelter.
  • It is not a stable (a stable is for horses).
  • It is not an animal shelter or pound (those are government or charity facilities that house stray or abandoned animals, whereas a kennel is privately owned and usually focused on dogs with owners).
A kennel is either (a) a small shelter built for a dog to sleep in, or (b) a professional facility where dogs are boarded, bred, or trained.
